(p-3745) Surah al-Hijr

It was named after its containing the words of Allah Most High: "And the companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers" (15:80), up to His words: "what they used to earn" (15:84). This indicates that they were held to account merely for denying the messengers and turning away from the signs of Allah, with the least degree of accountability, despite the utmost of their fortification. In it is the utmost magnification of the messengers and the signs. It is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an, as al-Mahayimi stated. It is a Meccan surah, and its verses number ninety-nine.

(p-3746) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words Most High:

[1] "Alif-Lam-Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an."

"Alif-Lam-Ra" (al-Ra): the discussion of its like has already passed. "These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an": the demonstrative refers to "Alif-Lam-Ra," because it is the name of the surah, meaning: these magnificent surah are the verses of the perfect Book and the verses of a Qur'an of great standing, clarifying (mubin) the judgment and the rulings, and the path of right guidance and error. It derives from (abana), the transitive form. Or its apparent meanings, or the matter of its inimitability, and its being a compelling sign, derive from (abana), the intransitive form. Or the demonstrative refers to the verses of the surah, or to all the verses of the Qur'an. The definiteness of "the Book" is for glorification and exaltation, like the indefiniteness of "Qur'an." And His words:

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[2] ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾

﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾ It is good tidings to the Prophet (ﷺ) of the manifestation of his religion, and that days will come in which the disbelievers will wish that Islam had preceded them, so that they would have been among the foremost (al-sabiqun). This is because they will see the exaltation of the word of the religion and its prevalence despite the atheists. For whoever embraces Islam later among them, even if he attains the virtue that he was promised, the best reward (al-husna), he will not reach the foremost: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the victory. Those are greater in rank.﴾ (al-Hadid: 10). In it is also a confirmation to the Prophet (ﷺ) to proclaim the call and to be patient in it, because the final outcome is his. The expression of diminution (sigha al-taqlil) was used in conformity with the practice of the Arabs in their saying "la'allaka sa-tandamu ʿala fi'lika" (perhaps you will regret your action), out of elevated dignity and self-sufficiency from explicitly stating the purpose, based on the claim of its manifestation.

﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves⁠﴾ means: with their worldly life and the fulfilling of their desires. ﴿And let hope distract them⁠﴾ means: it occupies them away from repentance and admonition, the hope that their state will remain sound, and that they will meet with nothing but good in the final outcome. ﴿They will come to know⁠﴾ means: for whom the good end (al-'uqba) will be.

﴿And they say, "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed you are mad."﴾ That is: O you who claim that! Then Allah the Exalted explained that they will not cease mocking the Messengers, even if there come to them the signs that would (ordinarily) compel (people to belief), because of the strength of their obstinacy and their transgression, through His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:

[14-15] ﴿And if We opened to them a gate from the heaven, and they continued ascending therein,﴾ ﴿they would surely say: "Our eyes have only been intoxicated; rather, we are a people bewitched."﴾ [al-Hijr: 15].

﴿And if We opened to them﴾ i.e., to these mockers, ﴿a gate from the heaven, and they continued﴾ i.e., they remained the whole day, ﴿ascending therein﴾ i.e., climbing up, seeking clarity regarding the wonders they would see therein.

﴿They would surely say: "Our eyes have only been intoxicated"﴾ [al-Hijr: 15] i.e., they were bewildered or their sight was blocked from seeing, and what we see is a thing we imagine, having no reality: ﴿rather, we are a people bewitched﴾ [al-Hijr: 15].

Al-Nasir said in (al-Intisaf): The purpose, and Allah knows best, of the two verses is establishing the proof against the deniers that Allah, the Exalted, has inserted the Qur'an into their hearts and made it enter their innermost hearts, just as He inserted it into the hearts of the believing, affirming ones. So these denied it and those affirmed it, each on the basis of knowledge and understanding: ﴿that whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives might live upon clear evidence﴾ [al-Anfal: 42], and so that the disbelievers will have no argument against Allah, saying that they did not understand the aspects of its inimitability as the one who believed understood them. Allah the Exalted informed them now, while they are in respite and capability, that they disbelieved only with knowledge, being obstinate, transgressive, and not excused, and Allah knows best. This is why He followed it with His saying: ﴿And if We opened to them﴾, the verse, i.e., these people understood the Qur'an and knew the aspects of its inimitability, and it penetrated their hearts and settled there, but they are a people whose nature is obstinacy and whose mark is contentiousness, such that even if one led them along the clearest path and the one most conducive to belief by way of necessary witnessing, namely by opening for them a gate in the heaven and having them ascend to it until they entered through it in daylight.

The indication of this is His saying: ﴿they continued﴾, because continuing (in ascent) occurs only in daylight; they would say after this great, manifest clarification: ﴿Our eyes have only been intoxicated﴾ [al-Hijr: 15], and Muhammad has bewitched us. These are merely imaginings with no realities beneath them. Thus I shall record against them that they have no excuse for denial, from lack of hearing, awareness, reaching the hearts, or understanding, as others among the believers understood, because all of that is available to them. Rather, obstinacy, contentiousness, and persistence are in them, and nothing else. And Allah knows best.

Then the Exalted explained the proofs of His oneness, His greatness and His dazzling power, by His saying (glorified be He):

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted be He:

[16–18] ﴿And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations (burooj) and adorned it for the observers. And We have protected it from every accursed devil. Except one who steals a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flaming fire.﴾ [al-Hijr: 17] [al-Hijr: 18]

﴿And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations (burooj)﴾: the plural of (burj), which is applied to a palace and a fortress, and to the twelve mansions through which the sun moves, in apparent vision.

The burooj in the verse have been interpreted as stars, as the aforementioned mansions, and as palaces, by way of comparison with the fortresses and palaces of the earth. Indeed the stars are magnificent, great structures. ﴿And We adorned it﴾, i.e., the sky, with those burooj of differing shapes and visible lights. ﴿For the observers﴾, i.e., those who look at their movements and their lights; or for those who reflect, take heed, and derive proof from them of the power of their Creator and His oneness.

﴿And We have protected it from every accursed devil﴾ [al-Hijr: 17]

﴿Except one who steals﴾ [al-Hijr: 18], i.e., snatches stealthily: ﴿a hearing﴾ [al-Hijr: 18], i.e., from the heavenly angels: ﴿and he is pursued﴾ [al-Hijr: 18], i.e., it follows him and overtakes him: ﴿by a clear flaming fire﴾ [al-Hijr: 18], i.e., a manifest, burning blaze, so that he either turns back or is burned.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 15, verse 19:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[19] ﴿And the earth — We have spread it out, and cast into it firm mountains, and caused to grow in it of every thing in measured proportion.﴾

﴿And the earth — We have spread it out﴾, i.e., We have laid it out flat. ﴿And cast into it firm mountains﴾, i.e., mountains that are steadfast. ﴿And caused to grow in it of every thing in measured proportion﴾, i.e., weighed by the balance of wisdom and determined by a measure that requires it, such that there is neither excess nor deficiency in it; or, in the sense of what is pleasing and well-proportioned, from their saying: "a speech that is mawzun" (balanced, measured).

Al-Sharif al-Murtada mentioned in (al-Durar) that the Arabs used it in this sense, as in the verse of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a:

"And a discourse I enjoy, which is of the kind souls desire; it is weighed out, weighing."

The commentary on the words of Allah the Exalted:

[20-21] ﴿And We have made for you therein means of livelihood, and [also] for those for whom you are not providers.﴾ ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.﴾ [al-Hijr: 21].

﴿And We have made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, i.e., that by which you live, of foods, clothing, and other things, which the necessity of life requires. ﴿And [also] for those for whom you are not providers﴾, i.e., of the livestock, the beasts, and what is similar to them. Al-Qadi (al-Qadi al-Baydawi) said: The summary (fadhlakah) of the verse is the argument from making the earth extended with a specific measure and shape, differing in its parts in position, producing therein kinds of plants and animals differing in creation and nature, while it is possible that it might not be so, [demonstrating] the perfection of His power and the consummateness of His wisdom. And [it contains] the singling out of Lordship (al-tafarrud fi al-uluhiyyah) and the bounty upon the servants through what He has bestowed upon them in that, so that they may affirm His oneness and worship Him. Then he emphasized this and said: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾ [al-Hijr: 21].

(p-3753) I.e., there is not a thing except that We are capable of bringing it into existence and producing it, multiplied many times over what has been brought forth from it. He likened His power over everything and His bringing it into being to treasuries in which things are deposited, prepared for bringing out whatever He wills from them, and He does not bring it out except in a known measure; this is a metaphorical allegory (istiʿarah tamthiliyyah). Or He likened His capabilities to stored things whose bringing forth requires no cost or exertion; this is an implicit metaphor (istiʿarah makniyyah). The meaning of ﴿We send it down﴾ [al-Hijr: 21] is: We bring it into existence and bring it forth into the world of witness (ʿalam al-shahadah). [20-21] ﴿And We have made for you therein means of livelihood, and [also] for those for whom you are not providers.﴾ ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.﴾ [al-Hijr: 21].

﴿And We have made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, i.e., that by which you live, of foods, clothing, and other things, which the necessity of life requires. ﴿And [also] for those for whom you are not providers﴾, i.e., of the livestock, the beasts, and what is similar to them. The meaning of ﴿We send it down﴾ [al-Hijr: 21] is: We bring it into existence and bring it forth into the world of witness (ʿalam al-shahadah). The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[22-23] ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing, then We sent down water from the sky and gave you drink from it, and you are not its storers.﴾ ﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors.﴾ [al-Hijr: 23].

﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ means: they fertilize the clouds, i.e., they make them carriers of water, because the cloud is vapour which, by meeting cold air, becomes a carrier of water. This is what al-Mahayimi (al-Mahayimi) said. On this reading, al-lawaqih (fertilizing) is the plural of mulaqqih (fertilizer) with the extra letters removed. Or they fertilize the trees by the flow of water into them, or by their growth so that they bear fruit and flourish. It is also permitted that al-lawaqih is the plural of laqih (pregnant), which is the pregnant she-camel. On this reading, the wind that brings the rain-laden cloud is likened to it, just as what is not like this is likened to the barren (al-'aqim), so it is said: a barren wind (rih 'aqim). ﴿Then We sent down water from the sky and gave you drink from it, and you are not its storers﴾ means: you are not capable of producing it or sending it down. Al-khazn (storing) is the making of storehouses, and it is used metaphorically for capability, as has passed. Or it means: you are not guardians of it in the places of its springs, of plains, mountains, wells and pools. Rather, He, Exalted is He alone, is the One who preserved it, routed it as springs in the earth, made it sweet, and showed mercy by providing it to drink.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 15, verses 26–27:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26–27] ﴿And We certainly created man from clay of dried mud, from black altered mud fashioned into shape﴾ ﴿And the jinn We had created before from the fire of the scorching wind﴾ [al-Hijr: 27].

﴿And We certainly created man﴾ means Adam. ﴿From clay﴾, i.e., dry clay that gives a ringing sound. ﴿From black mud﴾: this is an attribute of "clay", i.e., made of clay that has changed and turned black. ﴿Fashioned into shape﴾ means shaped (from "sanat al-wajh", which is its form), or poured (from "sanna al-ma'", meaning he poured it), i.e., molded into the form of a human being. It is as if He, glorified is He, poured out the black mud and shaped from it the image of a hollow human being, which dried until, when struck, it gave out a ringing sound. Then He turned it into a body of flesh and blood and breathed into it of His spirit.

﴿And the jinn We had created before﴾ [al-Hijr: 27], i.e., before man.

﴿From the fire of the scorching wind﴾ [al-Hijr: 27], i.e., from the fire of the intensely hot wind.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The context of the verse, as it stands, serves to show the perfection of His power, exalted is He, and to explain the beginning of the creation of the two weighty ones (humans and jinn). It is thus a reminder of the second premise on which the possibility of the Resurrection depends, namely the receptiveness of the materials to being gathered together and brought back to life.

﴿They said, "Do not be afraid. We give you the good news of a knowing boy."﴾ ﴿He said, "Do you give me good news although old age has touched me?"﴾ [al-Hijr: 54], meaning: despite old age having touched me, that a child will be born to me, while old age prevents it. ﴿Then of what do you give good news?﴾ [al-Hijr: 54]. Al-Zamakhshari said: the interrogative ﴿مَا﴾ (mā) here has acquired the meaning of wonder, as if he said: "By what wonder do you give me good news?" Or he meant: "You give me good news of something that is not conceivable in the normal course, so by what means do you give good news?" ﴿They said, "We have given you the good news in truth, so do not be of those who despair."﴾ [al-Hijr: 55], i.e., those who lose hope in that.

﴿He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?"﴾ [al-Hijr: 56], meaning: I did not deny that out of despair of His mercy, but out of deeming it unlikely according to the custom that God, Exalted is He, has established. And the explicit mention of "the mercy of God" is in its most fitting place.

**The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on verses 68–77 of Surah al-Hijr**

**Explanation of His words, the Exalted:**

[68–77] ﴿He said: "Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me. [p-3762] ﴿He said: "Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me."﴾ That is: by mistreating them, for mistreating them is a disgrace to the host.

﴿And fear Allah and do not humiliate me.﴾ [Al-Hijr: 69]

﴿They said: "Did we not forbid you from [harbouring] the people?"﴾ [Al-Hijr: 70] That is: from sheltering any of them, or defending them, or coming between us and them, for they used to molest everyone. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to rise to forbid evil and to stand between them and whoever molested them. So they threatened him and said: ﴿"If you do not desist, O Lut, you will surely be among those expelled."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 167] This is transmitted from al-Zamakhshari.

﴿He said: "These are my daughters, if you must act."﴾ [Al-Hijr: 71] The discussion of this has already been covered in detail in Surah Hud.

﴿By your life [la'amruka]﴾ [Al-Hijr: 72] is an oath by the life of the Prophet (ﷺ), inserted as an interjection expressing dismay at the intensity of their heedlessness and as an honouring of the one addressed. ﴿Indeed, they were in their intoxication﴾ [Al-Hijr: 72], that is, their heedlessness, which carried away their reason. ﴿Wandering blindly﴾ [Al-Hijr: 72], that is, hesitating, so that they did not understand what was said to them. When they did not heed his counsel, which would have preserved them, Allah made them hear the Cry that destroys them.

﴿So the Cry seized them﴾ [Al-Hijr: 73], that is, the Cry of punishment. ﴿At sunrise﴾ [Al-Hijr: 73], that is, entering the time of the sunrise.

﴿We made﴾ [Al-Hijr: 74], that is, by that Cry which shook the earth: ﴿its highest part its lowest﴾ [Al-Hijr: 74]. Al-Mahayimi said: because they made the men on top like the lowly women.

﴿And rained upon them stones of baked clay [sijjil]﴾ [Al-Hijr: 74], that is, hardened clay, as a stoning for their practice of sodomy [liwat].

﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern [al-mutawassimin]﴾ [Al-Hijr: 75], that is, those who look at the signs with insight.

﴿And indeed, it [wa-innaha]﴾ [Al-Hijr: 76] refers to [p-3763] the town of the people of Lut, which was destroyed: ﴿lies on an established road﴾ [Al-Hijr: 76], that is, a lasting way which people travel, and which has not yet been obliterated, while they still see those remains.

Al-Zamakhshari said: this is a warning to the Quraysh, like His words: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning﴾ [As-Saffat: 137] ﴿and at night. Will you not reason?﴾ [As-Saffat: 138]

﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers﴾ [Al-Hijr: 77], that is, in their destruction there is a lesson for them.

**Two admonitions:**

**The first:** Ibn al-Qayyim said in *Aqsam al-Qur'an*: most of the exegetes, from the early generation (salaf) and later ones, indeed the salaf knew of no dispute about it, hold that this, meaning His words ﴿By your life﴾ [Al-Hijr: 72], is an oath by Allah by the life of His Messenger (ﷺ). This is among his greatest virtues, that the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, swears by his life, and this is a distinction not known for anyone else.

Al-Zamakhshari was not successful in this, so he diverted the oath to mean that it is by the life of Lut, and that it is from the words of the angels.

He said: it is with the meaning of "saying", that is, the angels said to Lut, peace be upon him: ﴿By your life﴾ [Al-Hijr: 72], and so on. But there is nothing in the wording that indicates either of these two matters. Rather, the apparent wording and its context only indicate that what the salaf understood is more pleasing, not [the reading of] the people of ta'til (denial of divine attributes) and i'tizal (the Mu'tazila).

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: ﴿By your life﴾ [Al-Hijr: 72] means "your life". He said: Allah has not sworn by the life of any other prophet. Al-Amr and al-Umr are the same [in meaning], except that they reserved the oath for the form with the fatha (al-amr), to affirm the lighter [form], because of the frequency with which it occurs on people's tongues. Also, al-umr is a particular kind of life; so it is a noble, great life, worthy to be sworn by, because of its superiority over every lifespan of the children of Adam. There is no doubt that his life and his lifetime are among the greatest blessings and signs, so he is worthy to be sworn by. And swearing by him is better than swearing by any other created thing.

Then [p-3764] Ibn al-Qayyim said: Allah, glorified is He, described the people of Lut's sodomy as intoxication, because love has an intoxication like the intoxication of wine, as the poet said:

*Intoxicated: one intoxicated by desire, and one by wine. When will the one who is drunk with it sober up?*

**The second:** His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern﴾ [Al-Hijr: 75]. Al-Suyuti said in *al-Iklil*: this verse is the basis for *firasa* (physiognomy, discernment of character from outward signs). Al-Tirmidhi transmitted from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet: "Beware of the firasa of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah," and then he recited this verse. And some of the Maliki judges used to rule by firasa in legal matters, following the method of Iyas ibn Mu'awiya. End of quotation.

Al-Raghib al-Isfahani has excellently discussed firasa in his book *al-Dhari'a*, where he said in the seventh chapter: As for firasa, it is inferring a person's moral qualities, virtues and vices from his bodily form, appearance, colouring and speech.

It is sometimes said: it is a hunting art for knowing people's characters and conditions. Allah, may He be exalted, has indicated its truth by His words: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern﴾ [Al-Hijr: 75], His words: ﴿You will recognize them by their mark﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 273], and His words: ﴿And you will surely recognize them in the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad: 30]. Its word derives from their saying "the beast [faras] seized the sheep," so firasa is the snatching of knowledge. This is of two kinds. One kind occurs to a person from an impulse whose cause he does not know, and this is a kind of inspiration (ilham), indeed a kind of revelation, and it is what the Prophet (ﷺ) meant by his words: "The believer [p-3765] looks with the light of Allah." This is what its possessor is called: the one who is perceptive (al-mura''i) and the one who is spoken to inwardly (al-muhaddath). The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "If there is among this community a muhaddath, it is Umar."

Regarding His words: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil﴾ [Ash-Shura: 51], it is said that [this] is revelation by casting [something] into the heart (al-ru'). This applies to the prophets, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 193] ﴿upon your heart﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 194]. It may also occur by inspiration while awake, and it may occur during sleep. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "A true dream is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood."

The second kind of firasa is an acquired skill, namely knowledge of the relations between colours and forms, and between temperaments, morals and natural actions. Whoever knows this has a penetrating understanding through firasa. Books have been written on this, and whoever traces what is sound in them will find evidence of the truth of what they contain. Firasa is a kind of conjecture (zann). Some of the adepts among the Sufis were asked about the difference between them, and he said: conjecture is by the fluctuation of the heart, and firasa is by the light of the Lord. Whoever has the light of the Spirit strong in him, the Spirit mentioned in His words: ﴿And I breathed into him of My Spirit﴾ [Al-Hijr: 29], and who is among those described by His words: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord and is followed by a witness from Him?﴾ [Hud: 17], that light will be a witness, and he will be correct in what he judges. And among the instances of firasa is his (peace be upon him) saying concerning the two who engage in mutual cursing (li'an): "Indeed, their matter is clear, were it not for the judgment of Allah."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[97-99] "And We certainly know that your breast is constricted by what they say. So exalt [your Lord] with praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate [to Him]. And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty (al-yaqin)."

"And We certainly know that your breast is constricted by what they say. So exalt [your Lord] with praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate [to Him]. And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty." When He, exalted is He, mentioned that his people were mocking and deriding him, He informed him of what He knows of him, of the constriction and tightness of his breast because of what they say, for human nature and the human temperament necessitate that. Then He informed him of what removes the constriction of the breast and sorrow, namely His command to him of glorification (tasbih), praise (tahmid) and prayer (salat), as He, exalted is He, said: "And seek help through patience and prayer" [2:45], and He said: "Verily, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest" [13:28]. It is known that in turning to what has been mentioned there is the drawing down of divine support with victory and aid, due to His saying: "Indeed, God is with the patient" [2:153], and His saying: "So remember Me, I will remember you" [2:152], and His saying: "Indeed, God is with those who are mindful of Him and those who are doers of good" [16:128].

It has been narrated in his (ﷺ) characteristics that when a matter distressed him, he would resort to prayer, as an interpretation of what has been mentioned.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The embellishment of the sentence with emphasis serves to convey the affirmation of what it contains of consolation. In mentioning the title of Lordship (al-Rububiyyah), together with its addition to his pronoun (ﷺ), there is what is not hidden of showing kindness to him (ﷺ) and indicating the reason for the ruling, namely the command to glorify and praise. By "those who prostrate" (al-sajidin) is meant those who pray, by the figure of speech of mentioning a part to mean the whole. And "al-yaqin" (the certainty): death, for it is certainly bound to reach every living created being. The attribution of "coming" to it is to signify that it is directed toward the living, seeking to reach him. The meaning: remain in worship as long as you are alive, like His saying, exalted is He, in Surah Maryam: "And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I remain alive" [19:31].

It has been said: the intended meaning of "al-yaqin" is the punishment of these people and that what He promised would descend upon them. There is no doubt that it is among what is certain, but the intention of death from it is more preferable. What supports this is His saying, exalted is He, reporting about the people of the Fire: "They will say, 'We were not among those who prayed. Nor did we feed the poor. And we used to engage in vain discussion with those who engaged [in falsehood]. And we used to deny the Day of Recompense, until there came to us the certainty'" [74:43-47]. And what is in the Sahih from Umm al-'Ala', a woman of the Ansar, that when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered upon 'Uthman ibn Maz'un after he had died, Umm al-'Ala' said: "May God's mercy be upon you, Abu al-Sa'ib! My testimony about you is that God has honored you!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What makes you know that God has honored him?" I said: "May my father and mother be ransom for you, O Messenger of God! Then who?" He said: "As for him, certainty (al-yaqin) has come to him, and I indeed hope good for him."

Note:

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: This noble verse, which is His saying: "And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty" [15:99], is used as evidence that worship, such as prayer and the like, is obligatory upon a person as long as his intellect remains intact, as in the Sahih of al-Bukhari from 'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then lying on your side." It is also used to refute those from the heretics (al-malahidah) who held that the intended meaning of "al-yaqin" is knowledge (al-ma'rifah). According to them, whenever one of them attains knowledge, the obligation of religious duties falls from him. This is disbelief, misguidance and ignorance. For the prophets, peace be upon them, and their companions were the most knowledgeable of people about God, the most aware of His rights and attributes and what is deserving of exaltation, and yet they were, along with this, the most devoted in worship and the most constant in performing good deeds until the time of death. End of quote.

It has been said: the intended meaning of "al-yaqin" is the punishment of these people and that what He promised would descend upon them. There is no doubt that it is among what is certain, but the intention of death from it is more preferable. What supports this is His saying, exalted is He, reporting about the people of the Fire: "They will say, 'We were not among those who prayed. Nor did we feed the poor. And we used to engage in vain discussion with those who engaged [in falsehood]. And we used to deny the Day of Recompense, until there came to us the certainty'" [74:43-47]. And what is in the Sahih from Umm al-'Ala', a woman of the Ansar, that when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered upon 'Uthman ibn Maz'un after he had died, Umm al-'Ala' said: "May God's mercy be upon you, Abu al-Sa'ib! My testimony about you is that God has honored you!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What makes you know that God has honored him?" I said: "May my father and mother be ransom for you, O Messenger of God! Then who?" He said: "As for him, certainty (al-yaqin) has come to him, and I indeed hope good for him."

Note:

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: This noble verse, which is His saying: "And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty" [15:99], is used as evidence that worship, such as prayer and the like, is obligatory upon a person as long as his intellect remains intact, as in the Sahih of al-Bukhari from 'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then lying on your side." It is also used to refute those from the heretics (al-malahidah) who held that the intended meaning of "al-yaqin" is knowledge (al-ma'rifah). According to them, whenever one of them attains knowledge, the obligation of religious duties falls from him. This is disbelief, misguidance and ignorance. For the prophets, peace be upon them, and their companions were the most knowledgeable of people about God, the most aware of His rights and attributes and what is deserving of exaltation, and yet they were, along with this, the most devoted in worship and the most constant in performing good deeds until the time of death. End of quote.
